replies.author: Commercial_Yam_4712
replies.body:
Asked your question Claude Code, so this is not written by me:

Here is a detailed breakdown of how I built "Dead Manhattan" (a 3D post-apocalyptic web game), including the initial prompt, tech stack, and automated testing setup.

***

### 1. The Initial Prompt

It all started with a single prompt before going to bed. The goal was to build a full game overnight with zero human intervention:

> Create a real 3D game  
> - Open world  
> - A large city, like New York, with tall buildings, streets, etc.  
> - Post-apocalyptic atmosphere  
> - A character who can walk around freely – ideally a real 3D person  
> - Resident Evil-style gameplay with a pistol  
> - Real shooting effects  
> - Attacking zombies  
>  
> - Three.js for buildings and world is allowed if you can make it realistic  
> - No cheap shortcuts  
> - Where necessary, spawn multiple sub-agents to judge quality and ensure visual/animation fidelity is top-tier  
> - Pull this off alone! I want a result tomorrow morning when I wake up – context windows/tokens don't matter (don't stop, just keep going!)

---

### 2. Architecture & Technical Stack

To ensure high performance without a complex setup, the game was built using raw, modern web standards:

* **No Build Tools (Vanilla ES Modules & Three.js r185):**
  * **What it does:** Uses standard browser modules directly via import maps, skipping Webpack, Vite, or complex build steps.
  * **The Advantage:** Instant loading during development and zero deployment friction. You just host static files (`python3 -m http.server` locally or `nginx` on live servers).

* **Procedural World Generation & Instancing:**
  * **What it does:** Generates the city, buildings, interiors, car wrecks, and 37 prop types procedurally, grouping similar objects together in memory (Material Buckets / Instancing).
  * **Analogy:** Imagine building a LEGO city. Instead of opening a new box for every single brick, you keep a tray of identical bricks next to you and snap them into place instantly.
  * **The Advantage:** Drastically reduces draw calls, allowing a massive 3D city to run smoothly at high frame rates inside a standard web browser.

* **Deterministic Randomness (`ctx.rng(seed)`):**
  * **What it does:** Replaces standard random numbers (`Math.random()`) with a seedable random generator.
  * **The Advantage:** Every time you load a specific seed, the exact same city layout, enemy positions, and items generate. This makes bug reproduction effortless.

* **Asset Pipeline without Manual 3D Modeling:**
  * **What it does:** Character concepts were created via Gemini, turned into 3D rigged models via Meshy, animations retargeted from Quaternius UAL using custom Python scripts (`tools/retarget.py`), and minor props generated headless via Blender scripts.
  * **The Advantage:** Complete end-to-end automated asset generation without needing to manually sculpt or rig 3D models.

---

### 3. The Quality Engine (Automated Testing & Dev Tools)

The real secret to making an AI-generated game playable without crashing is the testing layer:

#### A. The Frame-Based Game Loop (`window.__game.step`)
* **Analogy:** Think of a movie projector. Instead of playing in real-time where lag or CPU spikes change the speed, the game advances strictly frame-by-frame on command.
* **What it brings:** Complete determinism.
* **The Advantage:** Time is stripped away from the wall clock. If a bug happens on Frame #432, running the test again to Frame #432 reproduces the exact same glitch every single time.

#### B. Automated Screenshots via Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP)
* **Analogy:** An automated camera operator standing in front of the game monitor.
* **What it brings:** Automated visual regression testing (`tools/shot.mjs`).
* **The Advantage:** The agent boots Chrome, waits for the game signal (`window.__renderReady`), takes snapshots, or passes `--steps` to render sequence frames. It lets the AI *see* its own progress without human supervision.

#### C. Smart Automated Diagnostics (`imgstat.py`, `diag_bugs.mjs`)
* **What it brings:** Automated visual and touch checks.
* **The Advantage:** 
  * `imgstat.py` analyzes screenshots to detect black screens, white screens, or featureless empty renders. If a texture breaks, the tool catches it immediately.
  * `diag_bugs.mjs`, `aim_probe.mjs`, and `jet_probe.mjs` simulate complex user behavior (like multi-touch gestures or aiming inputs) to catch edge-case input bugs.

#### D. Multi-Agent Development with Module Contracts (`docs/CONTRACT.md`)
* **Analogy:** Like 8 contractors working on different rooms of a house at the same time using a shared blueprint.
* **What it brings:** Parallel development without breaking code.
* **The Advantage:** 8 AI agents worked simultaneously against a strict API contract (`CONTRACT.md`). `main.js` imported non-core modules defensively using `try { import() }`. If one agent generated a broken module, the rest of the game still loaded and ran fine while the broken part was fixed in isolation.
